newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police kills three Islamists in south.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police kills three Islamists in south.

text.p: Police shot dead three suspected Moslem militants on Saturday after a four-hour gunbattle in southern Egypt, security source said.

They said police had received information about a militant hideout and clashed with the gunmen near Sheikh Saleh Basha village in the Minya province, some 240 km (150 miles) south of the capital Cairo.
The sources identified the militants as Sadawi Nomaan, 23, Yasser Younis, 20, and 19-year-old Walid Abdel Hafez.
All three are believed to be members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) which has been fighting to overthrow the government since 1992.
The Gama'a, and other Moslem militant groups, want to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state. They target tourists, officials, policemen and Christians in their campaign.
More than 1,000 people have died in the political violence and government crackdowns on the militants have largely contained their activities to the southern provinces.
In Cairo, security sources said that police had rounded up 41 suspected members of the militant Jihad group. Members of the group shot dead Egyptian president Anwar Sadat in 1981.
